172.t: Fort Worth trip personnel and the 1925 split
172.s: After a rest, Ridgley names the members who went to Fort Worth, says Celestin led while he was business agent, and notes the 1925 split into two bands.
172.ch: Silver Leaf and the Tuxedo Band
172.q: That went to Fort Worth. Paul Barnes, saxophone. Chinese, drummer. John Marrero, banjo. Simon Marrero, bass. Celestine, cornet. William Ridgely, trombone. Emma Barrett, saxophone. Piano.

172.t: Celestin leaving and returning; Buddy Petit leaving the band
172.s: Ridgley says Celestin played first cornet, left about three or four times and was always welcome back; others like Buddy left to start their own band.
172.q: Oh, Solistan was in my lifetime playing first. You see, Solistan leaving my band and I didn't care where he would go, I'd always have open for him. When he come back, well he got ready to come back to the band and they all well understood that. They never did try to keep them out. You know, if he…

172.t: Tuxedo orchestra and Celestin's brass band with the same men
172.s: Ridgley says the orchestra was his and the brass band Celestin's, with the same men playing both. They sent funeral and dance work to each other and split the difference.
172.ch: Faking parts and the Tuxedo bands
172.q: Both, huh? Both. Now, you see, the orchestra, that was my band. I'm taking care of that, the dancing. And the Millard and Herbert band was Celestand. See, he didn't bother the orchestra and I didn't bother the orchestra. If they'd come to me and want to play an old funeral or something like that,…

904.t: Joining the Tuxedo Band in 1923 under Celestin and Ridgely
904.s: Paul joins the Tuxedo Band, with Celestin as leader and Ridgely as manager; the talk touches on the few violinists left and the job at Tranchina's.
904.q: Yeah. But Celestan was the leader, the trumpet player, he was the leader, but Bebe Ridgely was the manager of the band. He took care of all the business. Did they have a violin in those days? Well, they were just about dying out. Pierron was the only one that I know of, Lef and Robichaux. They were…

904.t: Celestin's Original Tuxedo Band, My Josephine, and wearing tuxedos
904.s: The Tuxedo split between Ridgely and Celestin; Paul composes My Josephine, and they discuss the tuxedo dress and brass band.
904.q: Black Rag and so forth. But there was a confusion came up between Ridgely and Salastair concerning some of the money. The band broke, broke up. Salastair quit the band. In fact, the band actually didn't break, but Salastair quit the band. But John Marrera and Simon Marrera came to me and said that…

291.t: Ridgely and Celestin split the Tuxedo band
291.s: Barnes explains the break between Ridgely and Celestin over money and how he and others persuaded Celestin to form his own band with Jeanette Sullivan on piano.
291.q: Well that's the point I want to come to. In fact what went between those two people, none of us actually never do it, but it was something concerning a few dollars.

291.t: Leaving Rene for Celestin's Tuxedo band
291.s: An insurance collector urged him to join the society bands, so he left Rene for the Tuxedo band to make more money.
291.q: That was Celestad. Celestad and Pierron and they were big society bands, you see. And they'd make more money. So I joined Celestad's band, Tuxedo band. They'd heard Rene very much because he liked it so much. He hated it. But there was nothing you could do but I was making more money and everything…

55.t: Back with Papa Celestin; saxophonists and Lorenzo Tio
55.s: Bill returns to New Orleans, joins Celestin, and discusses pianists and the Tios.
55.q: out of Jack Sheen, like I told you. Yeah. With Risley. See? And then they left there. See? And Teo still stuck with Risley until things got good. Then he went, jumped over to Pete Ron again. Then he went to New York. And that's where he went to New York and he never did come back. Stay there. He…

55.t: Ridgley's Tuxedo band and the one-dollar split
55.s: Ridgley's early lineup and how the Tuxedo band split from Piron and Celestin.
55.q: But before that, Babe, Babe Risley always was managing. Babe, Babe Risley had Peter Borkard, no, and P-Rone on violin. I think, I know P-Rone was on violin. T-O on clanging, Risley on trombone, Celeste on conant, I think it's George Foster on bass, Ernest Rapinoe on snare drum. And who was playing…

174.t: Ridgley's Tuxedo Band name versus Celestin's
174.s: Dejan says there was no confusion between Ridgley's Tuxedo Band and Celestin's Tuxedo Band.
174.q: No I never heard no confusion about it. I never heard no confusion about it because I don't think Susie had copyright on it but when Ridgely made his band he called it Ridgely's Tuxedo Band. Yeah. And Celestad Celestad's Tuxedo Band. That's right, that's the name he went on, that's the way he…

625.t: Order of bands: Clark, Handy and the WPA, then Celestin
625.s: Allen and Trotter straighten out the sequence of Trotter's bands.
625.q: We were Celestan after Robert Clark. I was with Robert Clark. We were Celestan last.

197.s: Discussion of whether Celestin led two bands; Dejan explains the Ridgley and Celestin Tuxedo bands of the 1920s.
197.q: No, during the time I was with him, he was with the band. He was always with the band. He was always with the band.

801.t: Simon and John in Kid Rene, Celestin and Ridgley bands
801.s: Simon went from Buddy to Kid Rene to Celestin's Tuxedo band, while John was assistant manager and later sided with Ridgley after the split.
801.q: Bands around New Orleans? Yes. Well, he started from Buddy. He went with Buddy. Oh, they must have stood together for about twelve years. And from Buddy, he went to Rene. Kid Rene band. Stayed with them in front of us? He stayed with them all, long time. And he left Rene with Celestan Tuxedo band.
